name: What is the difference between wainscoting and full wall paneling?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between wainscoting and full wall paneling?

acceptedAnswer.text: Wainscoting refers to paneling that covers only the lower portion of a wall, typically extending about one-third to half the height of the room. It often features a cap rail and baseboard, adding architectural detail and protection to the lower wall. Full wall paneling, in contrast, covers the entire wall from floor to ceiling. Both offer aesthetic and protective benefits, but wainscoting is often chosen for a more traditional look or to add subtle character, while full paneling creates a more dramatic, encompassing design statement. Your choice depends on the desired visual impact and room style.
acceptedAnswer.description: Wainscoting covers the lower portion of a wall for architectural detail, while full wall paneling covers the entire wall from floor to ceiling, creating a more comprehensive design.
